article.title: Mass Spectrometry Proteomics of the Nanoparticle Corona Is Highly Dependent on Sample Preparation Protocol

source_scope.laboratory_anchor: Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland and Dublin City University
source_scope.biofluid: pooled human plasma from eight healthy donors
source_scope.biological_independence: one pooled material with four technical replicates per digestion protocol
prohibited_interpretations: The twenty columns are technical protocol replicates of one pooled material, not twenty independent biological samples.
The source is not an independent evaluator, protected lockbox or no-author scientific reproduction.
The source is not added to the frozen R3 training population or used for retrospective target/model selection.
A source-local OOD result cannot be called donor-level or cross-laboratory biological validation.
Contaminant, reverse and multi-target protein groups are excluded rather than collapsed or imputed.

quantification_contract.source_accession_policy: split Majority protein IDs on semicolons, remove CON__ tokens, retain only exactly one accession present in the frozen R3 feature table
quantification_contract.rank_eligibility: strictly positive finite LFQ intensity, Reverse and Potential contaminant flags absent, one uniquely mapped R3 target
quantification_contract.numeric_zero_policy: retain as NUMERIC_ZERO and exclude from rank; never impute
quantification_contract.missing_policy: retain blank/NA as SOURCE_NA or SOURCE_BLANK and exclude from rank; never impute

claim_boundary: This is a license-resolved, author-run, same-lineage-independent technical source audit. It supports a separately frozen exploratory OOD candidate but does not establish donor-level biological validation, independent evaluation, external scientific reproduction, adoption or scientific submission readiness.
